id_and_class.theory_title: Yogācāra's Mind-Only: How Store Consciousness Makes Experience Cohere Without External Objects
id_and_class.summary: Yogācāra, systematized by Asaṅga and Vasubandhu, holds that what appears as a world of external objects is nothing but cognition, and that the split between an experiencing subject and an independent world is a construction within consciousness. An eightfold model of mind explains how experience stays orderly, continuous, and shared without external causes: a store consciousness (ālayavijñāna) holds karmic seeds that ripen into experience, while a defiled mind builds the persistent sense of ‘I’. Meditative practice can transform this basis and reveal nondual awareness.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Experience as Cognition-Only, Grounded in Store Consciousness

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a dependently conditioned flow (the dependent nature) that presents itself as a subject facing objects. What is directly experienced consists entirely of appearances within cognition.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Bodies and the material world appear within cognition; on the dominant reading, mind-independent matter does not exist. The store consciousness takes one's own body and surrounding world as its vague objects.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (consciousness is the base that bears false superimposition, though as a conditioned, momentary flow, not a substance; on illusionist readings even the act of consciousness is constructed)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: The subject-object (grāhaka-grāhya) duality is a structure cognition takes on and mistakes for reality. All eight consciousnesses are intentional, and the defiled mind (kliṣṭamanas) continuously misreads the store consciousness as a substantial self. Dignāga and Dharmakīrti add that every cognition is aware of itself cognizing.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Colors, shapes, bodies, and the inside-outside distinction appear within a cognitively organized field. Experiences arise and have consequences, but they reveal nothing intrinsic about a mind-independent world.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Eight consciousnesses; karmic seeds (bīja) and impressions (vāsanā); a store consciousness that is neither an individual self nor a universal mental substance; three natures (imagined, dependent, perfected); multiple mind-streams.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Meditative practice and phenomenological analysis, plus argument. Dharmakīrti's co-apprehension argument (sahopalambhaniyama) holds that object and awareness are always apprehended together, so an object is never met as mind-external.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Six manifesting consciousnesses (five senses plus mentation) that arise intermittently and lapse in deep sleep; a seventh, the defiled mind, that generates the sense of ‘I’; and an eighth, the store consciousness, that runs subliminally and without interruption.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal appearance; synchronic unity; continuity across sleep and meditative cessation; sense of self; intersubjective agreement; karma and liberation.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Seed ripening in the store consciousness. Intentional actions deposit seeds that later ripen into perceptions, which accounts for when a perception occurs and what it contains without any external object.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Experience is a stream of momentary cognitions arising from seeds as conditions ripen. The store consciousness flows like a river of changing water, and it ceases at liberation through the transformation of the basis (āśrayaparāvṛtti), when the eight consciousnesses become four purified wisdoms.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Within distinct mind-streams. Shared worlds arise because separate streams carry similar seeds from shared past actions, which ripen in parallel.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Intentional acts condition future experience across lifetimes, and a morally neutral store holds the seeds of both wholesome and unwholesome states. The defiled mind's egoism colors ordinary awareness.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Multiple consciousnesses operate at once, which permits multisensory perception and makes the qualities of a moment appear as aspects of one conscious state.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Experience is representation without anything represented beyond it (vijñaptimātra). The imagined nature carves the dependent flow into real-seeming subjects and objects along the joints of language.
core_claims_and_evidence: Dreams show that ordered places, sequences, and bodily effects can occur without external objects, as Vasubandhu argues in the Twenty Verses.
Atomism fails, since imperceptible atoms do not resemble the extended objects experienced and aggregates cannot be ultimately real.
The store consciousness was posited, on Schmithausen's reconstruction, to explain how ordinary awareness re-emerges after absorption into cessation, when all conscious activity halts.
By the time one judges an object perceived, both object and momentary perception have ceased, which undercuts direct realism.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Meditative and phenomenological analysis combined with philosophical argument, within a soteriological framework.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Critics ask whether a continuous, rebirth-spanning store consciousness smuggles back the self Buddhism denies; Yogācāra replies that it ceases at liberation and so is no eternal substance. Solipsism is the sharpest internal pressure. Dharmakīrti allows an analogical inference to other minds, but Ratnakīrti argues it is verifiable only in one's own case. Madhyamaka thinkers treat the view as provisional, superseded by universal emptiness.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Scholars dispute whether Yogācāra is ontological idealism, epistemological idealism, or phenomenology that brackets ontology. Illusionist readings threaten the foundation the three-nature theory needs, and the burden shifts to explaining why cognition presents itself as a world at all.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: A distinctive idealism constrained by no-self: the fundamental consciousness is neither Berkeley's perceiving souls nor Hegel's absolute spirit. It is foundationalist where Madhyamaka is not, presenting itself as a middle way between Abhidharma realism and universal emptiness.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: The store consciousness carries karmic seeds across rebirths, so a mind-stream continues after the body dies, though no permanent self does and the store ceases at liberation.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: The whole model of mind is built for liberation: undoing the constructed self and world to realize nondual awareness.
